title: Layered Vegetable Biryani with Turmeric Yogurt
summary: A fragrant Indian-style vegetarian biryani layered with spiced vegetables, rice and a golden yogurt drizzle coloured with turmeric. It is warming, aromatic and perfect for a comforting dinner.
steps: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear, then soak it in fresh water for 20 minutes while you prepare the vegetables.
Mix the yogurt with 0.5 tsp turmeric, the lemon juice and a pinch of the salt. Set aside; this will give the biryani a saffron-like golden colour.

Heat the oil in a large heavy casserole over medium heat. Add the sliced onion and cook for 10–12 minutes, stirring often, until deeply golden at the edges. Lift out about one third of the onion for layering and leave the rest in the pan.

Add the garlic, ginger and chilli to the pan and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in the cumin, ground coriander, cinnamon, cardamom, remaining turmeric, bay leaves, black pepper and the rest of the salt.
Add the potato, carrot, cauliflower and green beans. Stir well to coat in the spices, then add the chopped tomato and cook for 5 minutes until it starts to soften.

Stir in the peas and 150 ml of the vegetable stock. Cover and simmer for 10 minutes, until the vegetables are just tender but not mushy. Remove from the heat and stir in half the chopped coriander and mint.

Drain the soaked rice. Bring the remaining 500 ml vegetable stock to a boil in a separate saucepan, add the rice, and simmer for 6–7 minutes until the grains are about two thirds cooked but still firm in the centre. Drain off any excess liquid if needed.

Spread half the vegetable mixture in the bottom of the casserole. Spoon over half the rice, drizzle with half the turmeric yogurt, and scatter with some reserved fried onion and herbs. Repeat with the remaining vegetables, rice, yogurt, onion and herbs.
Cover the casserole tightly with a lid and cook over very low heat for 18–20 minutes, until the rice is tender and fluffy and the layers are steaming. Rest off the heat for 5 minutes.
Gently fluff from the edges so the layers stay partly distinct, then serve hot with any extra yogurt if you like.
